diagram_classification: cosmological / meteorological (wind rose, with an anthropomorphic centre)
interpretation: The diagram is a twelve-part wind rose. A large outer circle is divided by twelve radiating lines. Each line runs from a small central circle to a triangular terminal on the rim, and each terminal is decorated with interlace knotwork. The twelve terminals are most plausibly the twelve winds, or twelve directions of the horizon, distributed around the circuit of the world. Their alternating yellow and blue-grey colouring suggests a grouping of the winds into two types or qualities. The yellow terminals fall at the top, bottom, left and right, so they probably mark the four principal directions. The blue-grey terminals are the intermediate winds. The human head in profile at the centre is probably a microcosmic or anthropocosmic figure: a man, or the earth or world, placed at the point from which the winds are measured, or on which they converge. The head is enclosed in a ringed circle that is itself coloured yellow and blue-grey. This links the central figure to the pattern of the winds around it. The whole figure therefore expresses an ordered correspondence between the human being at the centre and the winds or directions of the cosmos. The exact identification of the winds, and of the central figure, is not given in the image, because no legible labels are present.
evidence: Twelve radial lines run from the inner ring to twelve triangular terminals on the outer orange circle. The terminals alternate in colour between yellow at the four cardinal positions (top, bottom, left, right) and blue-grey elsewhere, which implies a hierarchy of principal and secondary points. The centre holds a human head in profile inside a yellow and blue-grey ring, so the person occupies the focal position. The radial symmetry, the circular frame and the placing of the body text around the figure all point to a schematic, non-narrative diagram. No labels are legible, so the specific names of the winds cannot be read, which limits the certainty of the interpretation.
